items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: Mike and I played on a Frank Sinatra record called “L.A. is my Lady”

ctx.x: Great. Thank you. We don’t have to spend a lot of time on this but can you describe what a typical studio session entailed? How do you get the phone call? How much do you know before you get there? And that kind of thing.

Well that’s a tough question to answer because there were — every one was so different. But how do you get the call — it was a lot less dramatic than you think although let me insert this story because it’s a good one. We were just talking about this record the other night. Mike and I played on a Frank Sinatra record called “L.A. is my Lady” — a whole © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

LP with Quincy Jones. It became pretty well known. There’s a short film out, I haven’t seen it in a long time, and Michael Jackson was planned to show up and they filmed the whole thing. And Mike and I were asked to do, they were going to put a long film out so a couple of guys came over to my apartment, Mike came over with a film crew and one of the questions was how did he get the call? And Mike made up a scenario, well we had gotten a call from — what was that club, I can’t think — Juli — Frank’s guy in New…
